free_tier.stated: Shrimp 1: 500 GB base + 1 GB/day automatic growth, $5/mo — i.e. it crosses 1 TB at ~day 500 and 1.87 TB at 4 years, on a fixed price. Shrimp 2: 500 GB + 2 GB/day, $7/mo. Lobster: 2 TB + 3 GB/day, $10/mo. Separate fixed line: Opossum 1 = 1 TB for $29/YEAR, Polar Bear 2 TB $48/yr, Killer Whale 3.5 TB $84/yr.

egress.terms: 12 TB/month (Shrimp) or 18 TB/month (Lobster) on 1 Gbps, included. Metered, not CF-covered.

tooling: KVM with root — SSH/SFTP/rsync/rclone-sftp. RaidZ2 HDD backend on the fixed line.
chaining: The genuinely interesting mechanic: this is 'free storage over time' priced as a subscription. Capacity is a function of tenure, so the chaining move is tenure, not accounts — a $29/year Opossum is 1 TB now and the expanding plans add 365 GB/year for free at fixed price. No free tier.
limits_note: Bandwidth is the real cap (12–18 TB/mo). Growth is 1–3 GB/day, so it is unusable for a 20 TB cold archive in year one — it is a decade instrument. Montreal location.
reliability_note: Long-running Canadian host with a heavy Black Friday presence on LET/NodeSeek; NodeSeek threads name it among the 'highly trusted' big-disk providers. RaidZ2 on the fixed line.
confidence_note: One page read moves it to documented.
